# Kammūpacayakathā (Kv 15.11)

**ID:** Kv 15.11

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kammūpacayakathā* (Kv 15.11) is a debate located in the fifteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The discussion centers on whether intentional action (*kamma*) and the accumulation of action (*kammūpacaya*) are distinct phenomena [Park 2007]. According to the commentary (*Kathāvatthuppakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*), the position distinguishing the two was maintained by the Andhakas and the Sammitīyas [Walser 2005; Park 2007]. They posited that karmic accumulation persists independently of volition, being dissociated from consciousness (*cittavippayutta*), karmically indeterminate (*abyākata*), and without an intentional object (*anārammaṇa*) [Nyanatiloka 2007; Walser 2005]. This model was formulated to explain the mechanism of karmic fruition (*vipāka*) across intervals of time without requiring karmic potential to intrude constantly into ongoing conscious processes [Waldron 2003; Park 2007]. The Theravādin interlocutor refutes this distinction, arguing that karma and its fruition cannot be severed from mental concomitants [Devdas 2004].

Scholars situate this debate within broader Indian Buddhist theories of action and result (*karmaphalasambandha*), noting that the Sammitīya concept of *upacaya* is functionally aligned with doctrines such as *avipraṇāśa* ("indestructibility") [Kragh 2006; Walser 2005]. SuttaCentral records a connection with the *Kukkuravatika Sutta* (MN 57), which is confirmed by DharmaNexus text-reuse matches identifying a long shared passage between Kv 15.11 (§13.4–13.10) and MN 57 (§10.2–10.9) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects substantial Pali-internal text reuse with other debates in the *Kathāvatthu* (notably Kv 8.9, Kv 1.1, and Kv 11.1), the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3, AN 4, AN 10), the *Paṭṭhāna* (e.g., Patthana 1.3, 11.10), and the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 1) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignment, DharmaNexus identifies segments shared with Tibetan translations, including the *Karmaprajñapti* (D4088) and the *Gaganagañjaparipṛcchā-sūtra* (D0148) [DharmaNexus].
